column2: req_desc

Deployment and readiness
The app serves pages and the `/api` prefix on one origin at `APP_PUBLIC_URL` and `GET /api/health` answers `200` once it is ready.

Public addresses answer
Each of `/`, `/plans`, `/enquiry`, `/community`, `/developers` and `/login` answers `200` with a non-empty page to a reader with no session.

Deterministic seed
The store holds exactly the seeded departments, tiers, accounts, role grants, tables, snapshots and requests in Seed data, once, and a re-read finds the same counts.

PostgreSQL holds every record
Every record lives in the PostgreSQL collections named in Store shape, and each seeded collection carries its rows there.

Tier grant table
`GET /api/tiers` answers a top-level array of the four tiers in grant order carrying exactly the allowances in the grant table.

One source for every allowance
The plan page states each tier's row allowance twice, and every figure it states equals the stored grant row the console refuses from.

Plan matrix page
`/plans` shows the four tiers as cards in grant order with a yearly and monthly toggle, then the same tiers again in a comparison table.

Department boundary on reads
An account with no role on a department is refused that department's rows, views, change log and snapshots at every address.

Refusal pages name the department
A refusal for a department the reader holds no role in names that department and is a page with a client-error status, never a redirect.

Roles granted per department
Role grants are stored per account per department, and an approved request leaves its grant in the store.

Bearer auth and open addresses
Every closed API address answers `401` without a session, while the open addresses answer without one.

Typed values at the write boundary
A decimal into an integer column, a string past 500 characters, a value outside a choice list and a non-member flag value are each refused `422` with nothing written.

Wrong-type refusal shape
A wrong-type refusal carries a reason and the field, names the column caption, and leaves the row exactly as it was.

One log entry per amended column
A successful update writes one change log entry per amended column, sharing one recorded moment and each carrying its own before and after value.

Contiguous log ordinals
Change log ordinals are contiguous from one within each table and never repeat or restart.

Contiguous column positions
Column positions are contiguous from one, and removing a column closes the gap.

Append-only change log
A log entry survives the deletion of its row and the removal of its column, every role on the department reads the log, and no role amends it.

Change log page
The change log answers newest first, at most twenty entries a page, and its console page lists the entries newest first.

Locked table refuses amendment
Every amendment of a locked table is refused naming the locking period, writes no log entry, and the table page shows the period in its lock banner.

Unlock writes nothing
Unlocking a table restores amendment and writes no change log entry, and the lock can be applied again.

Write boundary order
The write boundary checks role, then lock, then allowance, then type, and reports the first failure.

Frozen snapshots
A snapshot answers a frozen copy of its rows that a later amendment of the live table never changes, and its address refuses every amendment.

Snapshot retention
A snapshot older than its tier's retention is unreachable while the retained one answers.

Uniqueness and missing tables
A second snapshot for a published period is refused `409`, and a table slug that does not exist answers `404`.

Row allowance refusal
A table answer states its tier, its row allowance and its row count from the grant table, and a refused row write adds no log entry.

Allowance notice
A table at or above four fifths of its row allowance (a row count of at least 0.8 times the allowance) shows a notice stating the count beside the allowance in the caution colour.

Shared view allowance
Creating shared views past the tier's shared view allowance is refused.

Who decides a request
Only a steward of the requested department decides a request, and the requesting account is refused its own decision.

Approval grants the role
An approved request leaves a role grant for the requested role on the requested department.

One open request
A second open request by one account for one department is refused `409`.

Refusals are client errors
A type refusal, a department refusal and a lock refusal each answer a client-error status, never a server error or a silent success.

Sales enquiry
The enquiry form marks its four mandatory controls, a malformed work email is refused `422` naming `work_email`, and a message past 1000 characters is refused.

Newsletter subscribe
A repeat subscribe of one address answers success both times and records one row.

Not-found page
An address with no route answers `404` with the custom not-found page.

Table panel scroll
On a phone the table panel takes the sideways scroll inside itself while the page holds its width and the row title column stays against the left edge.

Table semantics and type scale
The table marks its column captions and row titles as header cells, renders values in Inter at 13px and captions at 12px, pads cells 8px by 16px at every width, and panels carry an 8px corner radius.

Five colour families
The console renders no more than the five colour families the palette names.

Accessibility bar
Every public address passes WCAG 2.2 AA checks with one first-level heading, keyboard focus shows a visible ring, and console controls on a phone are at least 24 by 24 CSS px.

Navigation drawer
Below the desktop breakpoint the navigation toggle reports its expanded state and opens a drawer that holds keyboard focus inside it.

No sideways scroll
No public address scrolls the page sideways at 320, 390, 768 or 1440 CSS px wide.

Reduced motion
Under a reduced motion preference no animation runs on the landing page or the console table page.

Owning department in view
The table list, one table and its change log each show the department that owns the table.

Bands on public pages
The landing page is a vertical stack of full width bands, each carrying one idea with open vertical space between them.

Colour carries meaning
Blue marks what can be pressed, orange an allowance running out and red a refusal or lock, and each console view carries at most one solid blue block in its body.

View filters, sorts and operators
The view builder never offers contains for an integer column or greater than for a flag column, a view's filters select the rows its table answers, and its sorts order them with tied rows keeping their insertion order.

Counts never leak
A reader's table list and row totals never include a table or row of a department they hold no role in.

Server-held controls
The source keeps every record in PostgreSQL, reads every allowance from the grant rows, and checks role, lock, allowance and type in one write path.

Session cookie shape
Sign in sets the session cookie `keystone_session` carrying `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax` and `Path=/`, that cookie alone opens the console and the closed API, and `document.cookie` never reads it.

Sign out ends the session
`POST /api/auth/logout` ends the session it was called with and no other, after which that cookie answers `401` on `/api` and the console page answers a refusal page rather than a redirect.

Session lifetime
A session is valid for twelve hours from its `created_at`, a session past its `expires_at` answers `401` on `/api` and refuses the console page, and a stale session row stays in the store.

Password rules on sign up
Sign up refuses a password shorter than 12 characters and refuses the four published obvious passwords whatever their letter case, each `422` naming `password` and recording no account.

Sign up reveals no account
A sign up for an email already recorded and a sign up for a malformed email are refused with the same `422`, the same `email` field and the same reason word for word, and neither records an account.

Failed sign-in throttling
Five refused sign-in attempts for one work email inside fifteen minutes throttle that email, every further attempt for it answers `429` with a `Retry-After` header, a successful sign-in clears the count, and the throttle is keyed on the email alone.

One sign-in refusal
A wrong password and an email nobody holds are each refused `401` with the same reason, the same field and the same body word for word.

Form posts carry their token
A form-encoded post to the enquiry or the newsletter address carries the `form_token` its page issued, and one missing, empty or never issued is refused `403` naming `form_token` with nothing recorded.

Sign-in attempts are recorded
Every sign-in attempt records its work email, its moment and its outcome and never the password, and only a steward reads `GET /api/login-attempts` while every other role answers `403`.

Dialogs open from their own control
Each of the four console dialogs opens by pressing `Enter` on its own named control, carries that control's name as its own accessible name, and moves focus to a control it holds.

Tab stays inside an open dialog
While a console dialog is open `Tab` reaches only the controls of that dialog however many times it is pressed, and `Shift+Tab` on its first control moves focus to the last control of the same dialog.

Escape closes and focus comes back
`Escape` inside an open console dialog closes it and records nothing, and focus returns to the control that opened it, which held focus immediately before the dialog opened.

Keyboard-complete console flows
Saving a view, saving a row, deciding a request and publishing a snapshot are each completed with the keyboard alone, and each records its own result.

One region announces every result
Every console address carries one status region named `Workspace updates` whose sentence states the outcome of the last completed action in the published words.

Two boundaries and nothing between
The layout changes only at 640 and 800 CSS px, the three bands differ from each other, and inside one band the layout is the same at every width.

A closed drawer is unavailable
While the navigation drawer is closed its route links are hidden from the accessibility tree and take no keyboard focus, and opening the drawer returns them to both.

Notices keep their own timers
The saved-row affirmation and the refusal notice are the only timed notices, each staying for its published duration, a later action shows a notice an earlier timer already hid, an earlier timer never hides a later notice, and the standing allowance notice is never hidden by a timer.

The table updates in place
Applying a view, changing the sort and paging the rows each replace the rows without a page load, and the address carries the view, the sort and the page so a reload and a step back restore the same table.

The later change wins
When the filtering is changed twice in quick succession the table shows the later change's rows even when the earlier request answers last.

An open dialog stays reachable
At a phone width every control an open dialog holds is the element found at the centre of its own box, and a dialog taller than the viewport takes the scroll inside itself while the page behind it does not.

Every animation keeps its band
The drawer slide, the saved-row flash, the loading placeholder pulse and the staged row entrance each run inside their published millisecond band with the published per-row stagger, and reduced motion removes every one of them while the colour and the text still arrive.

Fixed copy reads exactly
The empty-table line, the refusal heading, the sign-out confirmation, the snapshot announcement and the not-found sentence each read on screen exactly as published, character for character.

Row versions climb by one
Every row carries a `version` starting at `1` that each accepted amendment raises by exactly one, and a `version` never decreases and never repeats on one row.

Stale amendments are refused
An amendment whose `If-Match-Version` header names a number other than the row's current `version` is refused `409` naming `version` and carrying `current_version`, and it writes no column and appends no change log entry.

Exactly one amendment wins
When several amendments of one row arrive together carrying the same `If-Match-Version`, exactly one of them is accepted and every other one answers the stale-version refusal.

Idempotent row creates
A create replayed with the same `Idempotency-Key` and the same body answers the first answer's body byte for byte and creates no second row and no second change log entry, while that key with a different body is refused `409` naming `idempotency_key`.

Double submit writes what is published
Two identical subscribes record one `subscribers` row, while two identical enquiry posts record two `enquiries` rows and two identical creates carrying no `Idempotency-Key` header create two rows each at a `version` of `1`.

An amendment is one unit of work
A `PATCH` naming several columns where one value is wrong for its column writes not one of the named columns, appends no change log entry and leaves the row's `version` where it was.

Derived table figures stay honest
A table answer's `count`, `stored_kilobytes` and `log_high_ordinal` are computed at the read and agree with the store after a create, an amendment, a delete and a column removal, with no gap and no repeat in the ordinals.

The change log is a hash chain
Every change log entry carries a `previous_hash` and an `entry_hash` built by the published SHA-256 recipe, the chain verifies from the first entry of each table, and no two entries of one table share a `previous_hash`.

Stable paging by cursor
A cursor walk of the rows endpoint answers every row that existed before it began exactly once in insertion order even while rows are created between its page reads, and a cursor issued for another table is refused `422` naming `cursor`.

Derived state is computed at the read
A table answer carries `read_at` from the server's own clock and a snapshot answer carries a `retained` ranked when it is read, and the store keeps no `retained` column and runs no sweep process.

Effective-dated tier grants
A department's tier grants each carry an `effective_at`, `GET /api/departments/{slug}/grants` marks only the grant in force `in_force`, and every allowance decision uses the grant in force at the moment of the write rather than a later grant that has not begun.

A snapshot records the rules it was published under
A snapshot records its tier, that tier's row allowance, content allowance and retention words at publication, and a later grant rewrites none of them.

The business time zone decides the day
Every period and retention boundary is decided in `Asia/Kolkata`, five hours and thirty minutes ahead of UTC and never UTC, so a `business_day` turns over at `18:30:00Z` and the turnover moment belongs to the later day.

Retention ranks and read-time expiry
A snapshot whose rank by `published_at` is at or below its tier's retention count answers `200`, the rank one above it answers `410` and is absent from `GET /api/snapshots`, and that expiry is computed at the read with no sweep process.

The session lifetime boundary is exclusive
A fresh session's `expires_at` is exactly twelve hours after its `created_at` to the second, and a session is refused at and after that moment rather than before it.

Content size is derived and floored
A table answer's `content_bytes` sums the published per-column contributions over its rows and `content_kilobytes` floors that figure by `1024`, both computed at the read, and the store keeps neither column.

The content allowance refuses the next write
A write to a table whose `content_kilobytes` has reached its tier's `content_allowance_kilobytes` is refused `422` naming the tier, the allowance and `content_kilobytes`, and appends no change log entry.

The department snapshot sequence is gap-free
Every snapshot carries a `sequence` contiguous from one within its department, with no gap and no repeat even when publishes for different tables of one department arrive together.

A snapshot's recorded figures never move
A snapshot's `row_count` and `content_bytes` are computed once at publication and answer the same figures after the live table is amended.

Deep paging and totals over a high-volume table
`actuarial-exposure` answers a page far from the first as its own slice, totals the rows under a filter in `X-Total-Count`, and sorts the whole table before the page is cut.

A page carries at most five hundred rows
A `per_page` above `500` is refused `422` naming `per_page`, and no rows answer carries more than `500` rows.

Steward-only administration console
`/console/administration` carries the `Grant administration`, `Access request queue` and `Sign-in attempt record` panels, only a steward reaches it, and a viewer, an analyst, an editor and a reader with no session each answer the published refusal rather than a redirect.

Permission is read again on every request
Every request reads the role grants standing in the store at the moment it is answered, so a grant revoked or created while an account holds a live session takes effect on that account's very next request rather than at its next sign in.

A grant authorises from its own moment
A role grant carries `authorises_from`, authorises nothing before that moment and authorises at it and after it, decided from the server's own clock when the request is read and with no sweep process.

A refused administration read records nothing
A refused administration request appends no administration log entry and records no `login_attempts` row, so the stream's highest `ordinal` and that record's count are both unmoved.

Bulk revoke is all or nothing behind its phrase
A mismatched confirmation phrase revokes nothing, changes no grant, appends no log entry and announces the published refusal sentence, while a matching phrase revokes every named grant or none of them when any one cannot be revoked.

Administration actions are attributed
Every grant created, grant revoked and request decided through the console appends one administration log entry naming the acting steward and the affected account, and that entry verifies in the published hash chain.

A steward governs one department only
A steward is refused `403` for every administration action on another department, `GET /api/admin/counts` counts no other department's rows, and a queue cursor issued for one department is refused `422` for another.

Only the published administration surface answers
An unaccepted method on an `/api/admin` address answers `405` naming `method` with an `Allow` header, a non-JSON administration write answers `415` naming `content_type`, and an unknown path under `/console/administration` answers the not-found page.

The request queue stays honest under concurrent decisions
The queue answers open requests ahead of decided ones by `raised_at` oldest first and twenty to a page, and when two stewards decide one open request together exactly one decision is recorded and the other answers `409` naming `state`.
`/app/run.json` holds string `install`, `build` and `serve` fields, and `serve` starts the production server in the foreground.
`/app/USER_README.md` lists the eight seeded account emails with their role, department and the password `deku-demo-pw-2026`.
Reserved `.browser_screenshots/` and `.downloads/` directories exist at the app root, empty.
